examples.title: Signal sources
examples.summary: The signal sources side by side: step, ramp, sine, pulse, and clock, plus a constant.

checks.why: on for the first 25 % of each period

examples.title: Arithmetic
examples.summary: Sum, difference, product, quotient, minimum, and maximum of a ramp and a constant.

examples.title: Math functions
examples.summary: Gain, absolute value, square root, sign, negation, and power of a sine; sine and cosine of time.

examples.title: Step responses
examples.summary: A unit step through a first-order filter, a second-order system, an integrator, and a delay; a ramp through a derivative.

checks.why: one time constant after the step
peak overshoot 1 + e^(−πζ/√(1−ζ²)) at t_p = π/(ωn√(1−ζ²))
settles at the step height: the ringing envelope is e^(−ζωn·1.9 s) ≈ 0.003

examples.title: Sampling
examples.summary: A sine held, delayed by one sample, and a step summed at a fixed sample rate.

checks.why: the 0.1 s sample, one period late

examples.title: Nonlinearities
examples.summary: Saturation, dead zone, relay, and rate limiter acting on the same sine.

checks.why: rising at 2 per second for 0.25 s

examples.title: Switches
examples.summary: A switch that follows a control signal, and a manual switch set by a parameter.

examples.title: Subsystems
examples.summary: A gain and a filter grouped into a subsystem with an input and an output port, next to an empty subsystem.

examples.title: Mux and Demux
examples.summary: Three signals carried across the sheet on one vector wire, then split apart again.

examples.title: Signal buses
examples.summary: Named signals bundled into a bus with a Bus Creator, and picked out by name with a Bus Selector.

examples.title: Logic gates
examples.summary: AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOR, and NOT on two Boolean pulse trains, and a Boolean turned into a number.

examples.title: Comparators
examples.summary: A sine compared with thresholds, with a ramp, and through a hysteresis band.

checks.why: on until the sine falls below −0.5

examples.title: Latch, timer, and sampler
examples.summary: Start and stop buttons set and reset a flip-flop, which times the run, gates a signal, and samples the start time.

checks.why: the clock at the start edge

examples.title: Thermostat
examples.summary: An on-off controller switches a 100 W heater to hold a room at 50 °C.

examples.title: PI and PID loops
examples.summary: The same first-order plant under a sampled PI, a continuous PID, and a sampled PID controller.

examples.title: RC and RL transients
examples.summary: A 10 V step charges a capacitor through a resistor, and another builds current in an inductor through a conductor.

examples.title: Electrical sources
examples.summary: Every voltage and current source driving a resistor, each with a voltmeter across it.

checks.why: −I · R: the current leaves through n

examples.title: Variable parts
examples.summary: A resistor, an inductor, and a capacitor whose values follow signals, and a potentiometer.

checks.why: Ψ = 1 V · 1 s over L = 3 H

examples.title: Op-amp amplifiers
examples.summary: Two inverting amplifiers: an ideal op-amp with a gain of −10, and a limited one that clips at its ±15 V rails.

examples.title: Controlled sources
examples.summary: Voltage- and current-controlled sources and a gyrator, each driving a 10 Ω load.

checks.why: 0.1 S × 1 V into p2, out of the load
1 S × 1 V gives 1 A, 10 V on 10 Ω

examples.title: Transformers and a saturating inductor
examples.summary: A coupled-inductor and an ideal transformer on a 10 V sine, and an inductor that saturates as its current rises.

checks.why: M/L1 × the 10 V peak, lightly loaded
the 10 V peak over the ratio 2
saturated at 10 A: close to 0.5 H × 1 A/s

examples.title: Battery, supercapacitor, and a heating load
examples.summary: A battery cell heats a temperature-dependent resistor while a power sensor measures it, and a supercapacitor charges at 1 A.

checks.why: V²/R of a full cell through its 5 mΩ into 4 Ω

examples.title: Switches and a breaker
examples.summary: An ideal switch, closing and opening switches, a two-way switch, and a breaker that opens an inductive circuit.

examples.title: Diodes and a Zener regulator
examples.summary: Three diode models rectifying a 10 V sine, and a Zener diode holding 5.1 V.

checks.why: a Shockley diode drops some tenths of a volt
Bv + Nbv·Vt·ln(i/Ibv): about 70 mA against the 0.7 A knee current

examples.title: Transistor switches
examples.summary: A CMOS inverter of an NMOS and a PMOS transistor, and NPN and PNP transistors switching loads.

checks.why: input high: NMOS on, output low
input low: PMOS on, output high
base low: off, no drop on R C
base low: the PNP sources current into its load

examples.title: Thyristor and GTO
examples.summary: A thyristor that stays on until its current falls to zero, and a GTO that turns off with its gate.

checks.why: latched on after the gate pulse
turned off at the current zero

examples.title: DC-DC converters
examples.summary: Buck, boost, and bidirectional half-bridge converters switching at 10 kHz with 50 % duty.

examples.title: H-bridge and single-phase inverter
examples.summary: An H-bridge driving an RL load with 75 % duty, and an inverter leg making 50 Hz AC from a split supply.

examples.title: Rectifier bridges
examples.summary: A diode bridge and a thyristor bridge fired at 90°, each feeding a 10 Ω load from a 10 V sine.

checks.why: not yet fired in this half-cycle

examples.title: Three-phase inverter
examples.summary: A two-level inverter makes 50 Hz three-phase current in a star-connected resistive load.

checks.why: no DC in a balanced phase

examples.title: DC machines
examples.summary: Permanent-magnet, shunt, and series DC machines on 100 V, with their shaft speeds.

checks.why: no load at nominal field: V / k
the damper is sized for the nominal point

examples.title: AC machines on the mains
examples.summary: Induction, permanent-magnet, and reluctance machines started straight from a 50 Hz supply.

checks.why: no load: slip close to zero

examples.title: Resolver and Hall sensor
examples.summary: A shaft turning at 10 rad/s read by a resolver, a Hall sensor, and an angle sensor.

examples.title: Three-phase loads
examples.summary: A 10 V three-phase supply into a resistive star load, a series R–L star load, and a capacitor bank in delta.

checks.why: 3 · (10 V)² / (2 · 10 Ω), constant in a balanced load
10 V / 10 Ω at the phase a peak
10 V / |10 + j10| Ω, 45° after the voltage peak
√3 × the capacitor current √3 · 10 V · ωC, peaking at the phase voltage zero

examples.title: Three-phase transformer
examples.summary: A Dy1 transformer with ratio 2 steps 100 V phase voltage down into a star-connected load.

checks.why: never above half of the 100 V input
about 50 V, peaking 30° after the input (Dy1)

examples.title: Rotational drivetrain
examples.summary: A torque step drives a motor inertia through a 2:1 gear and a shaft spring into a damped load, with every rotational sensor.

checks.why: twice the 1 N·m after the gear
1 N·m / 0.01 kg·m²: at first only the motor moves, as the shaft has not twisted yet

examples.title: Clutch, backlash, and rotational sources
examples.summary: A clutch that locks, gear backlash, a spring-damper coupling, and a load that steps its torque.

checks.why: the gap is not yet taken up
the load torque now equals the drive: it coasts down with τ = 2 s

examples.title: Wheel and rack
examples.summary: A wheel turns axle torque into force on a vehicle mass, and a rack and pinion turns speed into travel.

checks.why: F / d with m = 100 kg + J / r²

examples.title: Mass, spring, and damper
examples.summary: Two 1 kg masses on 100 N/m springs and 2 N·s/m dampers, pushed by 1 N, with every translational sensor.

checks.why: peak overshoot of a ζ = 0.1 system
F / m at the instant of the step
the wall end is 1 cm behind the mass end

examples.title: End stops and motion sources
examples.summary: A sliding mass that hits its stops, a mass pushed into an elastic stop, and masses driven by speed and position sources.

checks.why: starts at the wall position 0.1 m, travels the 5 cm free length, then compresses 10 N / 10⁶ N/m
follows the reference peak at 0.5 s

examples.title: Cooling a hot part
examples.summary: A 10 W part cools through a thermal resistance into a heatsink that convects and radiates to 20 °C.

checks.why: heatsink balance of convection and radiation, plus 10 W · 2 K/W
all of the 10 W flows to the heatsink
port a is 10 W · 2 K/W hotter than port b

examples.title: Magnetic circuits
examples.summary: A 100-turn winding drives flux through an air gap and a core, next to magnetic sources and a variable reluctance.

checks.why: the gap takes 10/11 of the mmf
1 mWb · 10⁶ A/Wb: the source drives its flux out of n into the reluctance
